definition: Pressure index runs from 0 to 1 and falls as the nearest opponent moves away: 1 at about 1 m, 0 at about 9 m. A reading of 0.7 or more means the nearest opponent was within about 3.4 m when the ball was played.
Confidence is the share of the information needed for a reading that was actually observed in that frame. Below 0.75, positions are partly estimated and the reading is marked with a dotted style.

short: completed pass moving the ball 15 m or more towards goal
definition: A completed pass whose destination is at least 15 m closer to the opposition goal than its origin, measured along the length of the pitch.

short: pass or carry that ends with the opposition in possession
definition: A pass, carry or touch after which the opposition's next action is a recovery. Set pieces and clearances out of play are excluded.

short: the set of options available at release
definition: The ring is every pass or carry option a player had at that moment, given positions on the pitch. Each option is scored by the value of where it ends, times the likelihood it succeeds.

short: value at arrival divided by the best option at release
definition: The value of the outcome when the ball arrived, divided by the score of the best option in the ring when it was played. The scale runs from 0 to 1.5. Shown as Gain. Bands: Low gain below 0.55, Partial gain 0.55 to 0.79, Most of the gain 0.80 to 0.94, Full gain 0.95 and above. Above 1.0 means a run made the outcome better than any option available at release.

short: area a team could reach first
definition: Each hexagon is shaded by which team could reach it first, given positions and speeds in that frame. Darker means a clearer advantage.

short: how valuable the ball is at each location
definition: A pitch-wide surface of how much possession at each location is worth to the team with the ball. It is shown per hexagon and is the same on every screen.

short: decision quality from event data, without positions
definition: When a match has an event feed but no tracking, Ponta can estimate decision quality from start and end locations and outcomes. It cannot rank alternatives, so it is shown as a range and never as a single measured score.

short: carry beginning within 10 s of a turnover and moving 20 m or more forward
definition: A carry by the team that has just won the ball, starting within ten seconds of the turnover and covering at least 20 m towards goal.
